story_type: destroyer missile launch filmed by cameras right beside the launch cells
hook: A missile fired a few feet from the camera.
narration: A missile leaves the deck of USS The Sullivans in a wall of fire.
The destroyer was off the coast of Virginia, testing how it would defend itself against a close attack from the air.
Each missile waits sealed in its own cell below the deck, and fires straight up through a hatch.
Cameras bolted to the deck caught the blast from a few feet away.
Seconds later, the missile was only a white trail curving across the sky.
The ship carries the name of five brothers who served on the same cruiser and were lost together in 1942.
outcome: The Sullivans launched its Standard Missile 2 and the missile streaked away over the Atlantic.
title: Missile fired a few feet from the camera
question_comment: Would you stand on that deck during a launch, or watch from the bridge?
